svg.aria-label: Lemma 4: the padding run for p covers bytes 15 minus p through 15, so byte 13 is inside the run exactly when p is at least 2; altering it leaves the intended length-two pattern standing and breaks every longer one
svg.text: Lemma 4: why altering byte 13 resolves every ambiguity, with no chance of error
A true in Phase 1 means only that P4 ends in well-formed padding of some length p + 1 ≥ 2. The run covers bytes 15 − p … 15.

svg.text: p = 1 is the intended hit · p = 15 fills P4 exactly · p ≥ 16 runs on into P3 · p = 43 is the largest admissible value
byte 13 lies inside the run ⟺ 15 − p ≤ 13 ⟺ p ≥ 2
so the intended p = 1 is the one and only pattern the alteration leaves standing
Three things follow, and none of them is probabilistic.
Byte 13 sits in P4, so the adversary sets it through Δ[13]; no key material is needed.
It works even past the block.
A run with p ≥ 16 extends into the uncontrolled P3, but byte 13 is inside that run too, so breaking it does not depend on P3.
It is a dichotomy, not a test that can fail.
Either the run stops at byte 14, or it covers byte 13. Lemma 3 makes each probe an exact predicate, so no error can creep in.
